# beacon_webhook (Resource)

An outgoing webhook endpoint for incident events, signed with HMAC-SHA256.

## Example Usage

```terraform
# Secret generated by Beacon and captured at creation.
resource "beacon_webhook" "alerts" {
  status_page = beacon_status_page.main.slug
  url         = "https://hooks.example.com/beacon"
}

# Or bring your own secret (16-255 characters).
resource "beacon_webhook" "internal" {
  status_page = beacon_status_page.main.slug
  url         = "https://internal.example.com/hooks/beacon"
  secret      = var.beacon_webhook_secret
}

variable "beacon_webhook_secret" {
  type      = string
  sensitive = true
}
```

<!-- schema generated by tfplugindocs -->
## Schema

### Required

- `status_page` (String) Slug of the status page this belongs to (e.g. `beacon_status_page.main.slug`). Renaming the page's slug is followed in place; moving to a different page is not supported (taint the resource instead).
- `url` (String)

### Optional

- `enabled` (Boolean) Defaults to `true`.
- `secret` (String, Sensitive) Signing secret (16-255 chars). Generated by Beacon when omitted and captured from the create response; the API never returns it again, so the value in state is the one from creation (or from your config). Imported webhooks have no secret in state. This is a sensitive computed attribute rather than a write-only one because write-only attributes cannot hold a server-generated value; mark outputs that use it `sensitive`.
- `status_component_id` (Number) Only send events for incidents affecting this component.

### Read-Only

- `id` (String) Numeric id.

## Import

Import is supported using the following syntax:

The [`terraform import` command](https://developer.hashicorp.com/terraform/cli/commands/import) can be used, for example:

```shell
# <status_page_slug>/<webhook_id>. The API never returns the secret, so imported webhooks have none in state.
terraform import beacon_webhook.alerts acme-cloud/7
```
